text: The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired. You knew instantly: it means the animal. For a machine, that was the hard part.
In 1890, the psychologist William James wrote: everyone knows what attention is. For computers, nobody knew how to build it.
In 2017, a team at Google showed that attention alone was enough. Their paper was called: Attention Is All You Need.
Here's how it works. The word it sends out a question. Every other word holds up a label. The better the match, the brighter the thread.
The scores become shares that add up to one hundred percent. So it borrows most of its meaning from animal.
Now change one word. Too wide. The threads swing to the street. Same word, new meaning, and the model gets both right.
And every word does this with every other word, all at once. A thousand words means a million comparisons, in every layer.
That's attention. Every word, asking every other word: are you the one I need?
